_raises: 19 Sep 2026 THE WEARABLE ART LEFT THE BUNDLE — the player total fell 1 385 447 → 1 206 156 B (98% → 85%) and NO CAP MOVED. src/lib/banana-engine.js held 103 wearables as inline SVG: a grid of <rect> elements, one per 10-px cell, spelling out x/y/width/height/fill every time. 195 804 B of it, 86% of the engine and about 15% of everything a player downloads — on the one file the park, the beach, the homestead, the rave, the builder, the inbox and the quest all import. imgFor() only ever turns the string into a data-URI raster, so the representation was free to change. The readable art moved to tools/wearart-source.js (outside src/, never bundled, never counted), it ships packed as src/data/wearart.js at 17 809 B, and src/lib/wear-unpack.js decodes it BYTE FOR BYTE — proven by tools/check-wearart.mjs in node and by tests/wearable-art.spec.mjs against the built, minified chunk in a browser. banana-engine went 215 309 → 36 018 B built. The park, the heaviest first visit in the world, went 532 → 357 KB raw. Mostly a PARSE win: the art gzipped about 10:1, so transfer only fell about 10 KB. 19 Sep 2026 town-shop. NEW 9000 — a SPLIT, not new weight. town-room reached 53 779 B of 56 000 (96%, 2 221 B left) and Trym asked for chunking, so the four cards — Pip’s shelf, the travelling stall, the night vendor and the notice board — moved into a lazy chunk loaded on the first card or a beat after the square settles. town-room came back to 49 238 B (88%) and the new chunk is 6 218 B; the boilerplate of a second module is the ~1.7 KB the player total went up by. town-room. STAYS at 56 000: the cap is what made the split happen and lowering it in the same change hides the win. 15 Sep 2026 town-room. 48000→56000 — the town’s night grew in one day of Trym’s play: ghosts every night, roamers with four facings, mischief (a ghost snuffs a lamp, tips a bin, drops litter) and avoidance, walk-over pickup, the burst — 47 456 B built at 99%. Raised by one round’s worth. 15 Sep 2026 totalBudget 1400000→1420000 — the same growth carried into the player-facing total (98%); the town is still a hidden page and no other line moved. 14 Sep 2026 totalBudget 1350000→1400000 — TOWN LIFE is a new system on a new area: town-room.js (31 281 built, its own lazy chunk) plus its approved words tipped the player-facing total 3 837 B over a ceiling set before the town existed. Raised by one chunk’s worth, not more; the town is still a hidden page and no other line moved. 14 Sep 2026 town-room. NEW 48000 — TOWN LIFE (Trym’s brief, 14 Sep): the town’s shared condition read off the TownRoom, the look per band, per-player problems, Pip’s shelf for the homestead, the day’s events, Curse Nights, ghosts and cursed objects, in one lazy chunk loaded after the square stands so town.astro’s own script keeps its 70000. Six data tables ride inside it (src/data/town/); the words come from src/data/copy/town-life.json the day they are approved and add their bytes then. HIDDEN page still (noindex, linked from nowhere), counted toward totalBudget like any area. 12 Sep 2026 town.astro_astro_type_script. NEW 70000 — the town centre prototype: the square, the arcade room and THE LIFE SYSTEM (town-life.js: the day clock, nine residents with days, the lane router, bubbles, litter, the window glows) at 53KB built. It is a HIDDEN page (noindex, linked from nowhere) so no player downloads it yet, but it counts toward totalBudget like any world area — when the town opens for real this is the line that guards it. 12 Sep 2026 pulse-shell. 120000→130000 — the Arcade reached HQ: an AREAS room in the World tab and the five boards (a tile per cabinet + the wipe row) in the ledger room, 1.3KB over the line. Admin-only: no player downloads it, and adminBudget stays 220000 (90%). 12 Sep 2026 town-games. NEW 50000 — the Arcade’s five games in one lazy chunk, loaded the first time a cabinet is tapped (the town’s own script stays under its cap); the plan said at most 50KB per game module. 4 Sep 2026 THE TOTAL SPLIT IN TWO. One number was measuring two audiences: Banana HQ sits behind a token and no visitor downloads a byte of it, yet its 173KB counted against the payload a PLAYER pays for — so the gate that guards the game was creeping toward red for reasons the game had nothing to do with. This was pre-registered in the pulse-shell note below on 3 Sep ("the first chunk to argue about"), not invented when it got inconvenient. totalBudget is now player-facing only and adminBudget caps HQ, so admin weight stays bounded and visible rather than excused. Checked for real waste first and found none worth having: the engine is genuinely shared (not copied into the four bundles that reference it), and kitchen/phone/quest/tutorial/sticker-core are already lazy. The one real find was world-quest — 56.7KB fetched on EVERY visit to all four world areas by players who had already finished it, because bootQuest() checks S.done only after the chunk loads. The done flag is read off bwq-c1 before the import now. 3 Sep 2026 pulse-shell. NEW 120000 — Banana HQ's Pulse 2.0, an ADMIN-ONLY lazy chunk behind a token that no player ever downloads. Most of it is the two event dictionaries (245 labels + 285 explainers) moved verbatim out of worker-pulse's template literal; they are hand-written source that cannot be regenerated, so they are weight worth carrying. It counts toward totalBudget even though it never reaches a visitor — if the total gets tight, this is the first chunk to argue about. 2 Sep 2026 homestead-kitchen. NEW 16000 - the kitchen + the tailor split out of the homestead main chunk (94%) into a lazy chunk loaded on the first stove/fire/tailor open. 2 Sep 2026 homestead-phone. NEW 34000 — the Banana Phone + animal card split out of homestead.astro into a lazy chunk (loaded on first phone/card open) so the yard's hot path stays under its 130k cap. 29 Aug 2026 pass.astro 38000→42000 — My Pass gained subscription management (see the membership state, cancel it, un-cancel it). Deliberate: the exit for a paid membership is not a thing to shave, and the page had 103 bytes of headroom left.
_doc: Per-surface JS budgets in BYTES, measured on the BUILT output (dist/_astro) — the static-import back door means source size lies; only dist tells the truth. Prefix-matched against chunk filenames. Current size + ~15% headroom at adoption (24 Aug 2026); raising a number is a deliberate act that belongs in a PR description, never a drive-by.
